Question: How can you get the red tinge out of fingernails after removing dark red polish?
Old_Answer: You should only use pure acetone to remove nail polish. You can buy it at a beauty supply store like Sally Beauty. The nail polish remover sold in grocery stores and stores like CVS and Walgreen’s isn’t worth buying. It’s diluted and for that reason alone, you can’t depend on it. When you remove polish, always use a cotton ball and make sure it’s wet with acetone — not wet enough to be dripping but wet enough to cover and wipe off your entire nail. I typically use one cotton ball for each hand. Also keep in mind that you should never - ever - wear nail polish for more than six days before replacing it with a new coat. And wait 24 hours between manicures — 24 hours after you remove last week’s polish. If after taking all of these steps, you still see a red tinge of color on your nails, then where is it? If it’s under your nails, then use a Q-tip with acetone there as well. If it’s stuck onto your cuticles, then again, using pure acetone should do the trick. If none of this works for you, then just let your nails grow out and clip them every week until your nails grow back from scratch. That typically takes about two months.
